title: Naturality of the acyclic-resolution comparison
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], $\mathcal A$ with enough injectives, and let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $F,F'$ be objects of $\mathcal A$ and let $r:F\to I^\bullet$, $r':F'\to I'^\bullet$ be resolutions by $v$-acyclic objects [def-sp-acyclic] (that is, $I^m=I'^m=0$ for $m<0$ and the augmented complexes $0\to F\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$, $0\to F'\to I'^0\to I'^1\to\cdots$ are exact). Let $h:F\to F'$ be a morphism and $\varphi:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ a morphism of complexes with $\varphi^0\circ r=r'\circ h$. Let $c_I^n:\mathcal H^n(v(I^\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}R^nv(F)$ and $c_{I'}^n:\mathcal H^n(v(I'^\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}R^nv(F')$ be the comparison isomorphisms of item 2 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] (induced by a morphism of complexes over the identity into an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]). Then for every $n\geq0$ one has $c_{I'}^n\circ\mathcal H^n(v(\varphi))=R^nv(h)\circ c_I^n$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma Tag 015E (derived-lemma-leray-acyclicity, line 5717), naturality of the canonical map for morphisms of bounded-below acyclic complexes

proof.text: Choose injective resolutions $s:F\to J^\bullet$ and $s':F'\to J'^\bullet$ with $J^q=J'^q=0$ for $q<0$. By the injective-resolution lift lemma, choose a morphism of complexes $b:J^\bullet\to J'^\bullet$ with $b^0\circ s=s'\circ h$. View $F$ as a complex concentrated in degree $0$; the augmentation $r:F\to I^\bullet$ is then a quasi-isomorphism of bounded below complexes which is a monomorphism in every degree (the augmented complex is exact, so $r$ is monic in degree $0$ and $H^n(I^\bullet)$ is $F$ for $n=0$ and $0$ otherwise), and likewise $r'$. Applying the lifting lemma along an injective quasi-isomorphism to $\alpha=r$, $\gamma=s$ (resp. $\alpha=r'$, $\gamma=s'$), choose morphisms of complexes $a:I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ and $a':I'^\bullet\to J'^\bullet$ with $a\circ r=s$ and $a'\circ r'=s'$, i.e. over the identities of $F$ and $F'$. The comparison maps $c_I^n$ and $c_{I'}^n$ are the maps on cohomology induced by $a$ and $a'$ followed by the identifications of the injective resolutions with $R^nv(F)$ and $R^nv(F')$.

source.place: Tag 015E, proof of the acyclic-resolution comparison and its naturality

proof.text: The two composites $b\circ a$ and $a'\circ\varphi$ are morphisms $I^\bullet\to J'^\bullet$ whose composites with the augmentation $r:F\to I^\bullet$ agree: both are $s'\circ h$. The augmentation $r$ is a quasi-isomorphism and is degreewise monic because the augmented resolution is exact. Applying the lift-uniqueness-up-to-homotopy lemma to $r$, the two composites are chain-homotopic.

source.place: Tag 015E, naturality argument: two lifts over the same map are homotopic

proof.text: Since $v$ is additive, applying $v$ to this chain homotopy gives a chain homotopy between $v(b\circ a)$ and $v(a'\circ\varphi)$, and therefore the induced maps on cohomology are equal. This uses the fact that homotopic maps of complexes induce the same cohomology map.

source.place: Tag 015E, passage from homotopic lifts to equal maps on cohomology

proof.text: By the injective-resolution formula for the functor $R^nv$, the map induced by $b$ on the cohomology of $v(J^\bullet)$ and $v(J'^\bullet)$ is $R^nv(h)$. Rewriting the equality from Step 3 with the comparison maps $c_I^n$ and $c_{I'}^n$ gives $c_{I'}^n\circ\mathcal H^n(v(\varphi))=R^nv(h)\circ c_I^n$ for every $n\geq0$.

lean.statement: theorem acyclicComparison_naturality (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] {X X' : C} {I I' : CochainComplex C ℕ} (ι : (CochainComplex.single₀ C).obj X ⟶ I) (ι' : (CochainComplex.single₀ C).obj X' ⟶ I') [QuasiIso ι] [QuasiIso ι'] (hI : ∀ n, F.rightAcyclic (I.X n)) (hI' : ∀ n, F.rightAcyclic (I'.X n)) (h : X ⟶ X') (φ : I ⟶ I') (w : ι ≫ φ = (CochainComplex.single₀ C).map h ≫ ι') (n : ℕ) : HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((F.mapHomologicalComplex _).map φ) n ≫ (F.rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution ι' hI' n).inv = (F.rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution ι hI n).inv ≫ (F.rightDerived n).map h

reviewed_lean.note: C,D abelian + HasInjectiveResolutions C; F additive + PreservesFiniteLimits; ι,ι' single₀→I,I' QuasiIso over CochainComplex C ℕ; hI,hI' rightAcyclic termwise; w = degree-0 compatibility; c = (rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution _).inv (iso is R→H, so inv is H→R, item 2 identity lift); square Hφ≫c' = c≫R h, all n:ℕ
